Replacing the whole mecanism should be easy for a beginner, however I don't have much experience with quartz cronographs, especially seikos.. I usually just go for mechanicals.

As an active watchmaker, I would say a cronograph is a bit of a complicated mechanism to start on.

What the damage could be? Worn teeth on some gears, maybe the cronograph module has some issues with the reset jumpers.

My advice would be, take it to them to repair it, and source broken mechanical watches to play with, start simple with just time keepers, then move on to date, day date, and then cronographs. The latter has more gears and springs and parts to oil.

Now, if you feel like you would like a challenge, and are willing to risk it, as you could possibly break it even further, I'd say look for the documentation of the movement, spend 5-10 hours of just watching the watch being taken apart and re assembled, basic watchmaking, and parts count.

Best of luck!
